eyebrow: AI Engineering Leadership & Architecture · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 14 · Technical Leadership & Influence

code:
You made your case. It wasn't
accepted. You now genuinely
support the team executing
the chosen direction --

not quietly resenting it while
waiting to say "I told you so."
caption: The second version isn't commitment. It's passive resistance wearing commitment's clothing.

eyebrow: Why re-litigating is worse than it looks
code:
Lose the debate in the review --
bring the same objection back in
a side conversation or a 1:1.

Doesn't just fail to change the
decision -- it teaches the team
every decision can be re-opened
through a side channel.
caption: Teams that can't trust their own decisions to stay decided move slower on everything.

code:
During the decision:
  make your case clearly, in writing --
  Alternatives Considered, or the ADR.

After the decision:
  voice it once more, to the
  decision-maker directly -- then commit.
caption: Preserved reasoning, one final word, then the commitment phase begins.

eyebrow: When escalation is the right call instead
code:
The test: if this decision is wrong,
is the cost one the team can absorb
and learn from --

or genuinely difficult to undo?

(security vuln shipping to prod,
 a real compliance violation)
caption: Absorbable cost: disagree and commit. Hard-to-undo cost: escalate, before execution proceeds.

subtitle: The harder version: an audience that doesn't share your vocabulary.
